title: Cufflinks and clock stolen during break-in at country home of Prince William and wife Kate, court hears | CNN
text:
Source: Reuters/CNN

Two men allegedly climbed a drainpipe to break into the country residence of Britain’sPrince Williamand his wife Catherine, a UK court has heard.

Norfolk Constabulary previously said police were called on Monday evening following a report of suspicious activity at a property on the royal family’s Sandringham estate in Norfolk, eastern England. The property was unoccupied at the time, police added.

Mirgen Doku, 34, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, were charged on Wednesday of “entering a dwelling with intent to steal” and “trespassing on a protected site.”

The two Albanian nationals were assisted by an interpreter for their appearance at Norwich Magistrates’ Court later Wednesday, days after the alleged break-in at William and Kate’s country home, Anmer Hall.

The pair are accused of stealing six pairs of cufflinks and a clock, the court was told, according to Britain’s Press Association. One of the cufflinks allegedly stolen was described to the court as “the Duke of Edinburgh’s cufflinks.”

The court also heard that the items were of a value that is unknown and that a third suspect has not been apprehended.

The court heard that police were called after motion senses were triggered on the estate and near a window of the home. Scuff marks were found on a drainpipe on the side of the building and damage was found on an exterior window frame of the dressing room, leading prosecutors to allege that the men climbed the exterior pipe before forcing entry into the property.

The games and conservation manager at the royal estate was on patrol when he spotted two men jumping through a hedgerow into a wooded area using a thermal spotter, according to PA. The pair were also accused of dumping the items in the woodlands while on foot.

Police previously said specialist resources, including police dogs, drones and the National Police Air Service helicopter, were deployed to assist with searches in the area after they received a call just before 6 p.m. (1 p.m. ET), according to PA.

Two men were subsequently arrested, the court heard.

Doku and Ndoci were remanded in custody by District Judge Matthew Bone, who told them they will appear in court again on Monday.

The Sun newspaper first reported that police were investigating a break-in at the Wales’ country home.

Although the family uses the property as a retreat for holidays and short breaks, their main home is on the Windsor Castle estate to the west of London.

A spokesperson for William earlier this week said they did not comment on security matters.

The news of the attempted break-in came as William visited Prime Minister Andy Burnham at the British leader’s office, 10 Downing Street, on Tuesday.

While the British royals often mingle with political leaders and government ministers at formal occasions, visits to Downing Street, the official residence of British leaders since 1735, are more infrequent.

The late Queen dined with Winston Churchill at “Number 10” in 1955 on the eve of his resignation and became the first monarch for possibly 200 years to attend a Cabinet meeting there in 2012 during her Diamond Jubilee year.

As heir, King Charles also made a number of trips to Downing Street to attend meetings and see how the government functioned, while William’s late mother Diana, Princess of Wales also visited almost exactly 37 years ago in 1989.
